expected.finding: **[P1]** Threshold detection still misses evidence accumulated through multiple pending archive PRs. In `.github/workflows/archive-and-recommend.yml`, each run compares the default-branch archive with only its own review. If a topic has one occurrence and two reviews each add another before either archive PR merges, both runs see only two occurrences and report no crossing. Merging both archive PRs later does not trigger this analysis, so the three-occurrence threshold goes unreported. Reevaluate recommendations when archive updates merge, with durable deduplication of tracking issues.

**[P2]** A failed PR creation leaves a branch that prevents recovery. The “Propose the archived round as a pull request” step pushes its deterministic branch before calling `gh pr create`, then suppresses creation errors. On retry, no open PR is found, so the workflow generates a new commit—including a different `occurred_at` timestamp—and pushes to the existing branch. That push is rejected as non-fast-forward, preventing both PR creation and the subsequent tracking-issue step. Reuse the existing remote branch when retrying PR creation, and surface failures instead of treating an unproposed archive update as successful.
